conventions: byte strings are 0x-prefixed lowercase hex; field elements and scalars that exceed 2^53 are hex strings; `expected.evm`/`expected.ton` name the §5.2.2 outcome of VerifyCertificate steps 1–12 on a fresh destination deployed with `pin` at `now_ms` (null where that flavor cannot express the vector). `now_ms` is the destination clock: block.timestamp (EVM) or now() (TON) in whole seconds, times 1000, so every `now_ms` is a multiple of 1000. `headers.invalid[].error` is the first violated check in the order Length, X1, X2 (inactive) or X3 (active), X4, X5, X6, X7; X6 includes the rule that a ROTATION header has height and generation at most 2^64 - 2, so that the successor's start height + 1 and its generation + 1 fit u64 (rows rotation_at_max_height and rotation_at_max_generation); the rows named `<a>_and_<b>` violate two checks and report the earlier one, one row per adjacent pair of that order. `headers.*[].destination` is what the destination model answers for a certificate that carries the header. A certificate row carries `forgery_evidence_id` only when its `m` (the message that was signed) is the `m` a verifier derives from its wire fields. The TON verification context is ton-mainnet with the placeholder minter account id 0x35…35. `flavor_specific_certificates` are certificates that one flavor accepts and the other does not pin (rows of the same shape, without the pairing details)

flavor_specific_certificates.description: members 0 and 1 listed under keys shifted by T and −T outside G1, with the genuine signature: neither key is in G1, the aggregate key is, and the pairing holds. EVM sees the aggregate only and accepts; the TON outcome rests on the per-key checks of BLS_FASTAGGREGATEVERIFY (null until the Acton harness pins them)
flavor_specific_certificates.label: signer_keys_outside_g1_cancelling
